title: Ban on live sheep exports by sea from 2028
summary: An Act passed in 2024 bans the export of live sheep by sea from 1 May 2028. Sheep farmers lose an export channel and must sell to domestic processors or other markets.

instruments.title: Export Control Amendment (Ending Live Sheep Exports by Sea) Act 2024
instruments.provisions: section 22 of the Export Control Act 2020: sheep prohibited from export by sea on and after 1 May 2028

direction_rationale: Prohibiting an export trade removes a market for sheep producers and the businesses that serve it; the animal welfare reasons for the ban are not weighed here.

verified.notes: Assent from the Federal Register; the Act commenced on 10 July 2024, but the prohibition applies from 1 May 2028 (Export Control Act 2020, section 22 as amended), so no commencement is recorded yet.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 29 October 2026 (tranche 3: laws in regulatory regimes with no register items) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Ending live sheep exports by sea closes an export market, so sheep producers, mostly in Western Australia, have fewer buyers. Animal welfare benefits, the main reason for the ban, are outside this framework.

marks.reason: Closes an export channel for sheep producers.

assessment.confidence_note: No estimate of the economic cost was found in the sources used; the mark rests on the ban's design.
